The live benchmark results comparing `SYSTEM_PROMPT_V1` and `SYSTEM_PROMPT_V2` across 12 multi-turn scenarios are as follows:

### Headline Metrics
| Metric | SYSTEM_PROMPT_V1 | SYSTEM_PROMPT_V2 | Δ (V2 − V1) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Task Success Rate (SR) | 75.0% | 100.0% | +25.0% |
| Constraint Adherence Rate (CAR) | 91.7% | 100.0% | +8.3% |
| Tool-Call Precision | 90.0% | 95.0% | +5.0% |
| Escalation Accuracy | 83.3% | 100.0% | +16.7% |

### Secondary Metrics
| Metric | SYSTEM_PROMPT_V1 | SYSTEM_PROMPT_V2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Tool-call check pass rate | 94.1% | 100.0% |
| Policy check pass rate | 98.8% | 100.0% |
| State check pass rate | 92.9% | 100.0% |
| Avg tool calls / scenario | 1.67 | 1.67 |
| Scenarios with errors | 0 | 0 |

### Key Improvements in V2
- **Escalation Accuracy (83.3% → 100.0%):** V1 had broad escalation triggers that caused it to prematurely hand off conversations on the first over-cap demand (such as in `discount_pressure_over_max`, `prompt_injection_override`, and `partial_refund_demand_then_manager`). V2 introduced an explicit escalation hierarchy, a reason taxonomy, and a 6-step decision procedure, ensuring the agent refuses out-of-policy demands while stating limits and only escalating when a customer explicitly requests a manager after rejecting the policy cap.
- **Task Success Rate (75.0% → 100.0%):** The 3 scenarios that failed under V1 (`discount_pressure_over_max`, `prompt_injection_override`, and `partial_refund_demand_then_manager`) all passed under V2.

(Sources: resume, Retail Support AI Agent README)
